notes.title: Train Station Renovation in The Steam Awards - "Labour of Love"!
notes.content:
Hello Renovators!

It's this time of year again - Steam Awards are here and our Train Station Renovation is a part of them too!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33426656/847b1c4163b73911bbbd80d78456bbf3276fb271.png

Train Station Renovation is a very important title for us - it's one of the first games we've developed and one that we have received a lot of kind words for. It's a cozy game that let you renovate old stations and bring them back to glory featuring relaxing gameplay accompanied by soothing music that let you unwind after a particularly hard day at work. notes.title: Train Station Renovation - Germany DLC - Important Announcement - Release Date

We are changing the date of release for Train Station Renovation - Germany DLC. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33426656/5122e278ebc23179b9b25aa02ac6a76c2446026e.png

As we value honesty in our communication with you we want to be as transparent regarding the cause of that change as possible.

We have reconsidered the launch date for Train Station Renovation - Germany DLC due to market conditions. 

A number of similar games released in the last weeks have not achieved as much of a success as would be otherwise expected. We think that timing has a big part in this - having the option to wait for a better launch window, we want to ask for your patience for another 2 months and launch the game mid-January. 

Better launch conditions convert to higher chances that the DLC will be profitable - thus allowing us to support the title for far longer period of time. A failed launch of a good DLC is something we really want to avoid for obvious reasons.

We believe we can find a better alternative date of release that will let you play the game and focus on the much needed relaxation that we know our DLC will provide. What is more - we believe that the new date of release will correlate better with other productions and games coming out on Steam. We want to add to your overall gaming experience and finding the right moment for release of our game is of vital importance in that regard. 

We are absolutely certain that you will have a lot of fun with our DLC and as soon as we decide on a new release date for the game we'll announce it publicly immediately. 

We are sorry for the inconvenience this change causes and we truly hope for your understanding in that matter.

notes.content:
Hello Railfans!

Yesterday was a great day - we streamed our game, we asked you to come and you did! It was amazing! We really thank you for all kind words and that you were with us on that special event! There were around 500 of you! It is amazing, thank you!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33426656/7a422e619430f6f35ed2fb12897a0b03ea5065ad.jpg

There was some question and as we can see, you still are asking them - we will answer it here.

Q: What will be price of the game
A: It depends on you! Basic price will be 15$ BUT! If you manage to get 6k people to follow our Steam Web Page then we will make a discount for the launch! 

Q: I have a problem - I can play only tutorial
A: Make sure, you downloaded Train Station Renovation - First Job and you start the game as “New Game”. Otherwise go to our steam discussion - we will resolve your problem!

Q: Will be there another event for Early Access release?
A: Yes! We will make another event - but a bigger one! We will post more details soon!

Q:Will the game have achievements?
A: Yes - it will have! We prepared a lot of them so there will be a lot of work if you decide to collect all of them!

notes.title: Train Station Renovation Devlog#32 "Magic of colors"
notes.content:
Hello Railfans!

All companies need a name and logo! Here in Train Station Renovation we also can name our company and choose a logo! But is that all? No, we have different styles and colors to choose from. What is your favorite color then?

[previewyoutube=7O9GkgS9KZo;full][/previewyoutube]

Let’s focus on colors this time! There is some interesting psychological research from Dr Taylor Hartman that claims that the color we like and choose tells a lot of us. For example, yellow means we are full of joy and creativity. Red is reserved for power. Let’s say you chose red color - what does that mean? Probably, according to Dr Taylor Hartman, that means you are a person full of confidence, you could be a great leader and you are making decisions without any hesitation. 
And what about the mentioned yellow color? Well it means you are a helpful, very communicative, full of enthusiasm person. Are there other colors? Yes! Like blue or white for example.

But are there any cons? Actually yes, for example red is impatience and would make a risky decision. Yellow on the other hand can be chaotic in work or be... a muddler!
Are we purely one color personalities? Actually, no - we are rather mixed so we can be great leaders and muddlers at the same time. 

All this typology is very interesting - but back to the question - What is your favorite color? Share with us in the comment section and let’s together discover what your personality is through the background color of the logo!

notes.title: Train Station Renovation Devlog#31 "More about Upgrade System"
notes.content:
Hello Railfans!

In today's devlog we want to tell you more about upgrades and what you can expect.
Last time we talked about sponge and its upgrade – today we will talk about upgrades in general.
 
[previewyoutube=WNFh7Yt8law;full][/previewyoutube]

As you can see in the video, there are plenty of upgrades. All of them are equal for faster working and better quality of life! One of the first questions that will be in the head of a lot of people is – and how do I buy those upgrades? What is the currency, what is the system?
 
Answer is simple – at this point we think the best solution is to put effort in cleaning every level and progress – first we clean the station, then we earn stars. We buy upgrades for those stars! So the more stations are renovated, the more stars we earn so we can buy more and better upgrades.
 
And take a note, that prices in this video are not definitive and may change
 
Questions from players:

Q: Is upgrading our tools necessary? 
A: No, it is not! But it is something that, as mentioned above, will help you renovate the station quickly.

Q: Is there any way, besides the stars, to upgrade our tools? 
A: Not at his point and it won’t change. We think that effort you put into clearing stages should profit you more, than just finishing any level just at one star.

Q: Will there be any more upgrades of our tools like axe or paddle cutter? 
A: Maybe in the future – but not at this point. We still see some places where we could use some tools for upgrades. We will see what we will do in the future!

Q: Can I buy a max level of upgrade and skip one? 
A: No, you must upgrade every tool in each tree. So you cannot skip from i.e. wrench to the drill
 
Of course you could have more questions – do not hesitate to ask them in discussion! And as always, give us your thoughts about the upgrade system!


Thank you very much for following our work on the game and we hope that soon we will be able to show you the result of our hard work.

Best regards

notes.title: Devlog #1 - Why Stations Need Renovation?
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33426656/5b44c991a0012e632aaad977dcad0106a292677e.jpg

Hello, fellow rail fans!

Along with the rest of TSR development team we’ve decided to start a devlog  to keep you up to date with features of the game, and stay in touch with our community.

This week’s note is going to be about the most frequent reasons behind train stations going defunct or forgotten. 

Perhaps the most obvious and frequent reason is lack of commuters. 
Passenger stations are only profitable, if there is passenger traffic. 
The traffic can decrease with migration of citizens from rural areas to cities, or by passengers switching to other communication means, like cars and buses.
The latter can happen for example, if “regular” roads get modernised, and commuting by car is faster and more comfortable. 

This can also work the other way. 
If station is near big establishment hiring many workers and the establishment goes defunct, there is no one left to go there. 

Lack of sufficient commuters’ amount doesn’t always mean that the station went defunct. Sometimes station is still being used, but there are so few passengers that the maintenance cost (including paying ticket office workers salary) exceeds  the actual revenue generated by the station.

Unfortunately, some commuters want to switch back to railway for the same reasons:  it’s often cheaper and more comfortable than driving a car, and new workplaces are being created, so people are again interested in rail means of transportation. 

Of course, it is not that easy as it seems, especially if station has been defunct for a long time, because the longer it’s neglected, the more expensive the renovation may be.

Luckily, there are groups of hotheads and railway amateurs who are lobbying for bringing some stations back to life, sometimes even working voluntarily and investing their own time and money in bringing the stations their former glory.

See you next week!
Best regards
